personaChat.introMessage:
Hi, I'm Mera, your personal news assistant.

To find news that actually matters to you, I need to know a bit about you. Where you live, what you do, hobbies you follow, stocks you track, where your family lives. Share as much or as little as you like.

If that gives you pause, good instinct. It's not wise to hand personal data to an app company. Mera is built differently: everything you tell me is saved on your device, not on our servers. Ask me how that works, or say 'help me set up' and we'll get started.

welcome.title: Welcome to Mera
welcome.subtitle: What this app is, in one minute.

what.headline: A news app that starts with you
what.body: Most news apps start with the news and hope some of it fits. Mera starts with you, then goes looking for the stories that touch your life.

not-a-timeline.headline: Not a timeline
not-a-timeline.body: Nothing here is ordered by what is popular or by whatever arrived last. Have a guess at what decides the order.

popular.label: Whatever most people are reading
popular.feedback: Not here. Popularity is somebody else's news.

yours.label: How much it touches your life
yours.feedback: That's it. Everything else is only a tiebreak.

newest.label: Whatever came in last
newest.feedback: Close. New stories do land near the top, but being new is not what earns the top.

you-first.headline: Three steps, and that is the whole app

steps.0: You say a few true things about your life.
steps.1: Mera turns them into things to go looking for.
steps.2: It reads the day's news and keeps what fits.

matching.headline: Your life, not your clicks
matching.body: A nurse in a small town and a nurse in a capital city get different news here. Not because one of them tapped more, but because different things actually reach them.

stays-here.headline: It stays on this phone
stays-here.body: Tap each one to see what that means.

about-you.label: What it knows about you
about-you.text: Your facts, your interests and what you have read are written to this phone and stay there. There is no copy of them sitting on a server.

what-leaves.label: What actually leaves
what-leaves.text: Short topic phrases, like "hospital staffing". No name, no account, nothing saying the phrase came from you.

begin.headline: Ready when you are
begin.body: Mera will ask you a couple of things. There are no wrong answers, and you can change anything later.

facts.title: Your facts shape your feed
facts.subtitle: Tell Mera about your life. It does the rest.

a-fact-is.headline: A fact is one true line
a-fact-is.body: "I am a nurse." "I live in Utrecht." "I have a small child." Short, true, about your life. That is the whole idea.
a-fact-is.ask: What counts as a fact in Mera?

where-from.headline: Where facts come from
where-from.body: You never have to fill in a form.

steps.0: You talk to Mera and it listens for the durable bits.
steps.1: You tell it outright: "I moved to Lisbon."
steps.2: You add or remove them yourself on the You tab.

to-topics.headline: Facts become things to look for
to-topics.body: "I am a nurse" turns into several search phrases: hospital staffing, nursing pay, health policy. One fact fans out into a handful. Those phrases are what go out to find news.

sort-them.headline: Which of these is a fact?
sort-them.body: Tap a card, then tap where it belongs.

importance.headline: Some facts matter more than others
importance.body: On the You tab, open your facts and tap anything Mera knows about you to raise or lower how much it counts, reword it, or remove it. Turning something down is gentler than deleting it, and usually the better first move.
importance.ask: How do I change how important one of my facts is?

your-profile.body: Everything Mera uses to pick your news, in one place. Tap each one.
your-profile.headline: Your profile

facts.label: Facts
facts.text: The true lines about your life. Each one finds its own topics.

places.label: Places
places.text: Where you live, work and travel. They bring local news and add their countries to World.

show-less.label: Show less of
show-less.text: Topics you turned down inside a fact. Mera shows fewer stories about them.

sources.label: Sources
sources.text: Publications you want more or fewer of, and the ones you pay for.

feed.title: Reading your Feed
feed.subtitle: Where the day's stories live, and how they move.

two-lists.headline: Two views, one Feed
two-lists.body: The Feed shows the stories Mera picked for you. Continuous feed is one long list, the most relevant near the top. Sectioned feed groups the same stories by fact. Stories, a swipe away, keeps the developing stories you follow.
two-lists.ask: What is the difference between Continuous and Sectioned feed?

nothing-removed.headline: Nothing is ever removed
nothing-removed.body: Read a card and it does not vanish; it sinks. It is one continuous list, not sections cut off by dividers. Cards quietly drift down past the newer ones as you go.

steps.0: Leads: everything you have not seen yet.
steps.2: Lowest: already read. No divider, just a lower spot in the same list.

beforeAfter.before: Before you read it: the card sits up top with everything else that is new.
beforeAfter.after: After you read it: the same card, still there, just sorted further down the list. Scroll down and you can read it again whenever you like.

what-counts-as-read.headline: "Read" is broader than you think
what-counts-as-read.body: Tap at least two to see what counts.

open.label: Opening it
open.text: Tapping through to the full story counts, which is no surprise.

dwell.label: Just looking
dwell.text: A card that sits properly on your screen for a second and a half counts too. A fast scroll past does not.

act.label: Acting on it
act.text: A thumb, a save, following the story, or sending it to Mera all count as read.

order-holds-still.headline: The order holds still while you read
order-holds-still.body: Mera works out the order once, when you open the app or pull down to refresh, and then leaves it alone. Nothing rearranges itself under your thumb halfway down the list.

why-this-one.headline: Why this one?
why-this-one.body: Each card carries a short line saying why it reached you, and a word for how much it seems to matter. If a reason looks wrong, that is the single most useful thing you can tell Mera about.
why-this-one.ask: Where does the reason underneath a story come from?

quiet-by-design.headline: A quiet feed on purpose
quiet-by-design.body: Mera does not count at you while you read. Tap both to see how each view stays quiet.
quiet-by-design.ask: Why does the Feed not show how many stories came in?

feed.label: The Feed
feed.text: The Mera button moves while Mera reads and stays still the rest of the time. It is the only sign that anything is being fetched.

dashboard.label: Interests
dashboard.text: The same day sorted by interest, with a section for each thing you told Mera and unread stories first. Sections reorder when you leave the page, or every 10 minutes.

continuous.label: Continuous feed
continuous.text: The Mera icon at the top changes colour while Mera reads and stays still the rest of the time. It is the only sign that anything is being fetched.

sectioned.label: Sectioned feed
sectioned.text: The same stories grouped by fact, one section for each thing you told Mera, with unread stories first.

caught-up.headline: Running out is fine
caught-up.body: When there is nothing new left, Mera says so and stops. It will not pad the list to keep you scrolling. Everything you have already read is still below, if you want it.

teaching.title: Teaching Mera
teaching.subtitle: Two thumbs, one reason, and an undo.

two-thumbs.headline: Two thumbs
two-thumbs.body: Every story has an "I like it" and a "Not for me". They are the fastest thing to tap, and on their own the least useful.

bare-thumb.headline: A thumb on its own is thrown away
bare-thumb.body: This surprises people, so it is worth saying plainly.

steps.1: A small card opens and asks what it was about.
steps.2: Say nothing, and nothing is saved.

bare-thumb.ask: Why does a thumbs down on its own not change anything?

the-reason.headline: The reason is the useful part
the-reason.body: Which of these actually changes your feed?

just-thumb.label: A thumbs down and nothing else
just-thumb.feedback: Nothing changes. Mera cannot tell whether it was the subject, the source, or just today.

thumb-plus-reason.label: A thumbs down plus "too much about this football club"
thumb-plus-reason.feedback: That is the one. Now there is something specific to act on.

undo.headline: Undo is always right there
undo.body: Every change made from feedback shows a short confirmation with an Undo beside it. Tap that and it is as though nothing happened.

it-adds-up.headline: Small corrections beat big ones
it-adds-up.body: You do not have to fix your whole profile in one sitting. Two or three honest corrections across a week move the feed further than one long session ever does.
it-adds-up.ask: How soon does my feedback show up in the feed?

privacy.title: Your privacy
privacy.subtitle: What leaves this phone, and what never does.

stays-on-phone.headline: The part about you never leaves
stays-on-phone.body: Your facts, your interests, your places and everything you have read live on this phone. There is no copy on a server, which is also why signing out or switching phones means building the profile again.

what-leaves.headline: What actually goes out
what-leaves.body: Three things, and that is the list.

steps.0: Short topic phrases, so there is something to match stories against.
steps.1: How you sign in, by email or by this phone, and which plan you are on.
steps.2: A count of how many stories were analysed today, to keep that plan honest.

what-leaves.ask: What does the app send to your servers?

cloud-is-default.headline: The default is encrypted cloud
cloud-is-default.body: Reading a day of news takes a fair amount of thinking, and most phones would rather not. So out of the box that work happens in the cloud.

beforeAfter.before: The version we would love to tell you: your phone does all of it, always.
beforeAfter.after: What is actually true: by default the thinking happens in the cloud, encrypted on this phone and opened only inside a sealed enclave. On-device is a switch you can flip. We would rather say so than let you assume.

on-device-option.headline: On-device, if you want it
on-device-option.body: In Settings → Mera Protocol you can move the processing onto this phone. Then the AI that reads your news runs here instead of in the cloud. Your topic phrases still go out to fetch news, and signing in still needs your email or this phone. It downloads a model first, wants a fairly recent phone, and is noticeably slower, which is exactly why it is not the default.

what-we-keep.headline: What we do keep
what-we-keep.body: Your login email, if you added one. Which plan you are on. A per-day count of stories analysed. If you use Mera without an email, a sign-in record for this phone, deleted with your account. The topic phrases are cached by their text alone, with nothing recording who asked for them, and dropped after fourteen days unused.
what-we-keep.ask: What does Mera store about me on its servers?

following.title: Following a story
following.subtitle: Keep one story in view as it unfolds.

what-it-is.headline: For stories that are not over
what-it-is.body: An election, a trial, a storm, a takeover. Follow it once and every new development gathers in one place instead of arriving scattered through your feed over three weeks.

two-ways-in.headline: Two ways to start
two-ways-in.body: Both end up in the same place.

steps.0: On an article, open the ••• menu and tap Follow this story.
steps.1: Or tap the Mera button and say what you want to keep up with.

two-ways-in.ask: How do I follow a story?

pick-the-scope.headline: How wide should it be?
pick-the-scope.body: Mera offers three or four scopes and you tap one. Nothing is followed until you do. Which would you pick for a court case?

narrow.label: Just this trial
narrow.feedback: Tight and quiet. You will get the verdict and not much else.

medium.label: This trial and the appeals around it
medium.feedback: A good middle. This is the one most people want.

wide.label: The whole scandal it came out of
wide.feedback: Broad. You will get plenty, including things only loosely related.

the-timeline.headline: It gathers, it does not nag
the-timeline.body: New developments collect on the story's own timeline with a small count beside it. If the story goes quiet, Mera says so rather than inventing an update to fill the space.

stop-following.headline: Stopping is one tap
stop-following.body: Open the story and stop following. The gathered timeline goes with it, so if you only wanted a break it is worth knowing this is a delete rather than a pause.
stop-following.ask: What happens to the timeline if I stop following a story?

explore.title: World
explore.subtitle: The same headlines everyone else gets.

unscored-on-purpose.headline: Deliberately not about you
unscored-on-purpose.body: World is the one place Mera does not personalise anything. No scoring, no reasons, nothing learned from what you open here. Just what each country's newsrooms are leading with, in their order.

the-chips.headline: One page per country
the-chips.body: Mera builds the pages for you, and you can change them.

steps.0: World comes first unless you move it.
steps.1: Then your own country and the countries of your places, and after those, any country you added yourself.

the-plus-chip.headline: Adding a country
the-plus-chip.body: Where do you add a country to World?

places.label: Your places
places.feedback: Your places add their countries on their own. For any other country, press and hold a page name in the World header.

sources.label: A long press on a World page name
sources.feedback: Right. Press and hold a page name, then search for the country and add it.

settings.label: Settings
settings.feedback: No. Settings is a page of the You tab, and countries are not there.

search.headline: Searching the news
search.body: The search icon in the World header looks through recent headlines, roughly the last two days, not an archive. It is for "what happened with that thing", not for research.

hide-a-chip.headline: Too many countries
hide-a-chip.body: Press and hold a page name, then tap the x on a country to hide its page. If the country comes from one of your places, the place stays in your profile and only the page goes.
hide-a-chip.ask: How do I remove a country page from World?

sources.title: Choosing your sources
sources.subtitle: Badges, arrows, and the one control that is a block.

where-it-lives.headline: Where sources live
where-it-lives.body: One screen for every publication you adjusted.

steps.1: "Fewer from" in an article's ••• menu takes effect at once, with Undo, and the publication then shows under Adjusted.

where-it-lives.ask: Where do I manage which sources I see?

the-two-badges.headline: Only two badges exist
the-two-badges.body: Tap each one to see what it means, and what the absence of one does not mean.

government.label: Government source
government.text: The publisher is a government body. Worth knowing when you are reading an official statement about an official thing.

regulator.label: Official agency
regulator.text: A regulator or public agency: a health authority, a transport safety board, a central bank.

everything-else.label: No badge at all
everything-else.text: Everything else, which is nearly everything. It is not a quality rating, and its absence says nothing bad about a publisher.

arrows-on-a-publisher.headline: The same arrows, one publisher at a time
arrows-on-a-publisher.body: Open a country and every publisher has its own pair. Down is a nudge rather than a wall: a downranked publisher still turns up when it has a story nobody else has.
arrows-on-a-publisher.ask: What is the difference between turning a source down and muting it?

mute-is-not-a-downrank.headline: Mute is a different thing entirely
mute-is-not-a-downrank.body: Mute lives only on the source preferences screen, and it is a hard exclusion: those stories are dropped, not merely sorted lower. Tap each card and put it where it belongs.

steps.2: Either can be cleared later, from source preferences.

three-shelves.headline: Three shelves on one screen
three-shelves.body: The Not interested screen holds everything you have asked Mera to keep back.

steps.0: Words and things you have hidden.
steps.2: Sources you have muted or turned down.

three-shelves.ask: Where can I see everything I have filtered out?

exact-match.headline: A filter matches one thing exactly
exact-match.body: Filters are not searches. A place filter matches that place; a source filter matches that source. They compare an exact value against one field of a story, which is what makes them predictable, and also what makes the next card matter.

made-from-a-story.headline: Where the precise ones come from
made-from-a-story.body: You want to stop hearing about one particular place. What actually works?

type-it.label: Type the place name into the filter screen
type-it.feedback: That gets stored as words rather than as a place. Useful, but looser than you meant.

from-an-article.label: Say it about a story you are looking at
from-an-article.feedback: Yes. Tell Mera in chat, or use the feedback card on the story itself. The filter is minted from that story's real place, so it lines up exactly.

typed-is-words-only.headline: Typed filters are words
typed-is-words-only.body: You can add one by hand and it is genuinely useful: it catches a phrase wherever it turns up. It simply cannot be a place or a source, because a name you typed would almost never line up exactly with the stored one.

soft-fades-hard-stays.headline: Some fade, some stay
soft-fades-hard-stays.body: It depends on how firmly you said it, not on where it came from.

beforeAfter.before: A soft filter, "a bit less of this", steps aside after thirty days. Tastes move on.
beforeAfter.after: A firm one (the hard switch when you add a filter by hand, or muting a source) has no expiry at all and stays until you remove it yourself.

soft-fades-hard-stays.ask: Do the things I filter out ever come back?

chat.title: Talking to Mera
chat.subtitle: The fastest way to change almost anything.

where-mera-is.headline: Mera is on every page
where-mera-is.body: The round Mera button at the bottom right opens the chat, starting from the page you are on.
where-mera-is.ask: Where do I find the chat with Mera?

ask-what-it-knows.headline: Start by asking what it knows
ask-what-it-knows.body: "What do you know about me?" gets you the list it is actually working from. It is the quickest way to spot the one stale fact that has been quietly bending your feed for a month.

say-it-plainly.headline: Say it the way you would to a person
say-it-plainly.body: No commands, no syntax. Tap a couple of examples.

steps.1: Mera works out which settings that means.
steps.2: You confirm, or you do not.

less-of.label: "Less football, please"
less-of.text: Mera turns that into a turned-down topic and shows you the change before anything is applied.

more-of.label: "I have started cycling"
more-of.text: That becomes a new fact, and a few things to go looking for.

moved.label: "I moved to Lisbon"
moved.text: The old place is retired and the new one added, usually as one proposal you confirm once.

nothing-until-you-tap.headline: Nothing happens until you tap
nothing-until-you-tap.body: When Mera decides something should change, it stages the change as a card and stops. So what happens if you type "yes, do it" instead of tapping the card?

applies-immediately.label: It applies the change
applies-immediately.feedback: It does not. Typed agreement is not consent here; the tap is.

waits-for-your-tap.label: Nothing. The card is still sitting there waiting
waits-for-your-tap.feedback: Right. The card usually offers a choice of scope that only you can make, so it waits for the tap.

nothing-until-you-tap.ask: Why did Mera not apply the change I said yes to?

written-down.headline: Every change is written down
written-down.body: Applied changes are recorded with what it was before, what it became, and where the change came from: chat, feedback, a suggestion, or you. Nothing Mera does to your profile is invisible.

take-it-back.headline: And most of it can be taken back
take-it-back.body: The record lives in Settings → Mera Protocol → Persona change log.

beforeAfter.before: A weight change, an added topic, a filter you removed: these carry a Revert that puts things back exactly as they were.
beforeAfter.after: A few cannot be undone and say so: deleting a fact during a cleanup, or removing a place, throws away what would be needed to restore it. Those sit in the log with no Revert beside them.

take-it-back.ask: How do I undo something Mera changed about my profile?

protocol.title: The Mera Protocol screen
protocol.subtitle: A few switches, and what each one really does.

one-screen.headline: Where the switches are
one-screen.body: A few taps from anywhere in the app.
one-screen.ask: Where is the Mera Protocol screen?

processing-mode.headline: Processing mode
processing-mode.body: Where the thinking happens. Tap both.

cloud.label: Cloud (the default)
cloud.text: Your data is encrypted on this phone, opened only inside a sealed enclave, and encrypted again on the way back. Fast, and works on any phone. The app does not yet check that enclave's certificate against the chip maker, which the privacy notice says out loud.

on-device.label: On-device
on-device.text: Everything runs here and nothing about you leaves at all. It downloads a model first, wants a fairly recent phone, and is noticeably slower.

inject-noise.headline: Noise injection, still being built
inject-noise.body: Sending invented topics out alongside your real ones would make the phrases arriving from your phone harder to read as a portrait of one person. It is the part of the Mera Protocol we are still building: it is not built yet, so there is no setting for it and nothing pads what your phone sends today. We would rather tell you that than let you assume a protection you do not have.

web-search.headline: Web search in chat
web-search.body: Off by default. Turned on, Mera can look something up mid-conversation. What leaves your phone when it does?

whole-question.label: Your whole message
whole-question.feedback: No. And while the switch is off, the search tool is not even offered to the model, so it costs nothing at all.

search-words-only.label: Only the search words
search-words-only.feedback: Right. The words it decided to search for, and nothing else.

web-search.ask: What leaves my phone when web search in chat is on?

the-change-log.headline: The change log lives here too
the-change-log.body: Persona change log, on the same screen. Every change to your profile in order, newest first, with a Revert on the ones that can be undone. If your feed has drifted somewhere odd, this is where you find out when it happened.
the-change-log.ask: How do I see what has been changing my profile?
